communication_job: open inquiry, invite reflection or orient an interview
claim_boundary: The examples show question-like language in transcript context. They do not prove audience engagement, comprehension, turn-taking success or a universal benefit.
practice_hypothesis: Choose the question type that matches the job: invite reflection, open a narrative, check shared attention or request information. Do not use a question form to pressure a listener or disguise a claim.

representative_examples.title: ENGLISH SPEECH | OPRAH WINFREY: Learn From Every Mistake (English Subtitles)
representative_examples.text: girl with a bucket and big heart could dothat, I wonder what I could do?
representative_examples.function_hypothesis: self-question moving from another person's example to the speaker's own possible action
representative_examples.boundary: The question is narrated reflection, not evidence of an audience reply.

representative_examples.title: ENGLISH SPEECH | MATTHEW MCCONAUGHEY: White House Speech (English Subtitles)
representative_examples.function_hypothesis: short rhetorical or conversational question-like reaction before the formal address
representative_examples.boundary: The form may be a reaction or rapport move rather than information-seeking inquiry.

representative_examples.title: ENGLISH SPEECH | SACHIN TENDULKAR: Be the Best (English Subtitles)
representative_examples.text: Why don't we start right at the beginning?
representative_examples.function_hypothesis: interview-opening question that invites a narrative answer
representative_examples.boundary: The transcript cannot by itself establish turn ownership, prosody or whether the answer followed as intended.
